nodes.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
nodes.label: 5.NBT.A.3

nodes.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form , e.g., 347.392 = 3 × 100 + 4 × 10 + 7 × 1 + 3 × (1/10) + 9 × (1/100) + 2 × (1/1000).
nodes.label: 5.NBT.A.3a

nodes.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form . Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons. *Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.
nodes.label: 4.NBT.A.2

nodes.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.
nodes.label: 5.NBT.A.1

nodes.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model. *Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.
nodes.label: 4.NF.C.7

edges.reason: The earlier concrete money/length treatment gives useful tenths experience. The later node itself introduces tenths and hundredths as decimal fractions, so the link is spiral preparation rather than a distinct necessary concept; Gemini equates reintroducing that content with mandatory prior instruction.
edges.scope: extending decimal meaning from tenths to hundredths

edges.reason: Repeated decimal addition motivates multiplication by an integer and supplies checks. Computing the integer product then placing the decimal point does not execute a decimal-addition algorithm.

The source explicitly first computes an integer product before replacing the decimal point. Multi-digit integer by one-digit products are a component in that scope; the claim does not make a column layout exclusive for every multiplication.
edges.scope: integer multiplication before placing the point
